title: Verbs and nouns
summary: Combine d, c and y with any motion, and use the one-key edits x, r, J, ~, p and P.

steps.title: Operator + motion
body: vim editing is a tiny language: an **operator** (verb) followed by a **motion** (noun) says what to do to which text.
| Operator | Means |
| `d` | delete (and keep it in a register, so it is really *cut*) |
| `c` | change: delete, then enter insert mode |
| `y` | yank (copy) |
| `>` / `<` | indent / outdent |
```text
dw     delete to the start of the next word
d$     delete to the end of the line      (shortcut: D)
c$     change to the end of the line      (shortcut: C)
dt)    delete up to (not including) the next )
d3w    delete three words   (3dw does the same)
y}     yank to the end of the paragraph
dgg    delete from here to the top of the file
Doubling an operator acts on the whole line: `dd`, `cc`, `yy`, `>>`. Once you know 5 operators and 20 motions you know 100 commands.
> **Practise:** open **Labs → Vim & nano trainer** and run this lesson's challenges until the keys come without thinking.

steps.prompt: Match the keys to the edit.
pairs: delete to the start of the next word
delete to the end of the line
replace the whole line with new text
delete up to the next comma, keeping it

steps.prompt: The line is `let total = price * qty;` and the cursor is on the `p` of `price`. You type `dt;`. What is the line now?
steps.explain: `t;` moves up to just before the `;`, so `d` deletes `price * qty` and keeps the semicolon.

steps.prompt: The line is `timeout=30s` and the cursor is on the `3`. You type `cwPT45S` then `Esc`. What is the line now?
steps.explain: `cw` changes from the cursor to the end of the word (`30s`), then you type the replacement.

steps.title: One-key edits and paste
body: | Key | Does |
| `x` | delete the character under the cursor |
| `r` + char | replace the character under the cursor (stay in normal mode) |
| `~` | toggle the case of the character and move right |
| `J` | join the next line onto this one (with one space) |
| `p` | paste **after** the cursor (or **below** for whole lines) |
| `P` | paste **before** (or **above**) |
`dd` then `p` moves a line down; `ddkP` moves it up; `xp` swaps two characters; `yyp` duplicates a line.

steps.prompt: Does it leave you in insert mode?
The line is `teh` with the cursor on `e`. Which keys fix it to `the`?
steps.explain: `x` cuts `e` (cursor lands on `h`), `p` pastes it after the `h`.

steps.prompt: Copy the current line and put two copies of it below.
steps.explain: `yy` yanks the line; each `p` puts a copy below the cursor line.

steps.title: Real keys: operator, count, motion
prompt: Delete `really really really ` with **one** command: an operator, a count and a motion. Get there first with a word motion.
Then, in the same trainer, try **One more worker** (`yyp`) and **Purge the debug lines** (`3dd`): the same grammar with other verbs.
steps.explain: `d3w` reads as *delete three words*. `3dw` does the same thing. Because it is one change, a single `u` undoes it and `.` repeats it.
